source.title: Label Noise SGD Provably Prefers Flat Global Minimizers
source.authors: Alexandru Damian; Tengyu Ma; J. Lee

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: Experiments test whether label-noise SGD moves networks from poor training-loss minima toward flatter solutions with better test accuracy, using trace of the Hessian as a proxy rather than the claim versions' specified measures.
record.gate_note: The paper tests label-noise SGD from two poor generalization initializations and reports test accuracy and trace-of-Hessian results. Its trace-based sharpness proxy is not the magnitude-aware perturbation measure in V7, and it does not test another listed version. Learning-rate values in the figures and the cited prior results are not separate rows.
record.test_reason: The study tests label-noise SGD's implicit regularization and recovery from selected poor minima, but none of V1–V8. Hessian trace is not V7's magnitude-aware perturbation measure; batch size is fixed in the recovery experiments. Random-label fitting constructs an initialization without the matched natural-label and held-out random-label comparisons required by V1.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the empirical conclusion: label-noise SGD escapes both selected poor initializations, improves test accuracy, and reaches flatter solutions according to the reported proxy; regularization strength also varies with learning rate. The theoretical result establishes approximate stationarity near a regularized-loss stationary point under stated assumptions, rather than a general guarantee of improved held-out accuracy.
record.recipe_differences: The experiments use randomized label flipping with cross-entropy loss, ResNet18 on CIFAR10, no augmentation or weight decay, and compare trajectories from specially constructed poor minima. The claimed versions specify other interventions or measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors state that regularization strength is strongly correlated with learning rate. They also report different outcomes by initialization: the full-batch run reaches the baseline, while the adversarial run gets within 1%.

fits_no_version.finding: Label-noise SGD improves test accuracy from initializations with 76% and 48% test accuracy, reaching the random-initialization SGD baseline from the former and approaching within 1% from the latter. Accuracy tracks the reported Hessian-trace proxy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: On CIFAR-10 with ResNet18 using GroupNorm, randomized label-noise SGD can escape selected poor training-loss minima and improve generalization; a trace-based flatness proxy tracks this improvement.

record.problems: The experiments use one model and dataset, with three random seeds. The implicit regularizer is approximated by the trace of the Hessian. Results are shown across learning rates in figures, while the text gives no exact final accuracies for the label-noise runs or correlation coefficients.
record.rows_left_out: No additional eligible results omitted. Figure 3 and Figure 4 show trajectories across learning rates; the text does not give per-rate numerical values, so those values are not reconstructed as rows. Figure 4 reports momentum experiments, but the text does not state a separate outcome for them beyond referring to the figure.

untested.parts: Matched random-label and natural-label training with held-out accuracy measured for both; initialization construction alone does not supply this comparison.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under specified tuning and recovery conditions.
Held-out performance across batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout's effect on held-out error and interactions with dataset size, augmentation, and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance versus generalization gaps, including ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: Figure 3 and Figure 4 captions call the left panels training accuracy, but their axes and Section 4 identify test accuracy. Section 5.2 explicitly attributes improved momentum performance to stronger regularization; this still bears on no listed version. No verdict labels are warranted.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence across the specified architectures and datasets.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classification networks.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD and the stated tuning or recovery conditions.
Large versus small batch performance under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects and its interaction with data augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the effect on test accuracy.

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.operation_detail: Trained with label-noise SGD from the full-batch initialization.
rows.baseline: minibatch SGD baseline with random initialization; exact value not stated
rows.value: Reaches the SGD baseline from the full-batch initialization; exact value not stated
rows.uncertainty: Median over 3 random seeds; shaded error bars denote min/max over the three runs.
rows.note: The paper reports the comparison in text; no final accuracy number is stated for the label-noise run.
rows.check: Reports the study's method performance, not an effect named by a claim version. The reported recovery to baseline is accurate. Specify ResNet18 with GroupNorm, randomized label flipping probability 0.2, and learning-rate warmup. Appendix D specifies momentum and deterministic label smoothing when constructing the full-batch initialization.

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.operation_detail: Trained with label-noise SGD from the adversarial initialization.
rows.baseline: minibatch SGD baseline with random initialization; exact value not stated
rows.value: Gets within 1% of the baseline from the adversarial initialization
rows.uncertainty: Median over 3 random seeds; shaded error bars denote min/max over the three runs.
rows.note: The authors describe the result as within 1% of baseline, rather than reaching it.
rows.check: Reports the study's method performance, not an effect named by a claim version; being within 1% of baseline does not establish a partial effect for any listed version. The initialization memorized 500,000 pixel-masked, randomly labeled images before training on true CIFAR-10 labels. The no-augmentation condition applies to subsequent recovery training.

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.operation_detail: Measured the correlation between test accuracy and trace of the Hessian during label-noise SGD.
rows.measure: Correlation of test accuracy with tr ∇²L(θ)
rows.value: Strongly correlated in both cases; correlation coefficient not stated
rows.uncertainty: Median over 3 random seeds; shaded error bars denote min/max over the three runs.
rows.note: The trace is used as an approximation to the paper's implicit regularizer; this is not the magnitude-aware perturbation measure specified by V7.
rows.check: The reported accuracy–trace association cannot establish V7's magnitude-aware sharpness–generalization-gap relationship. No correlation coefficient is provided. Appendix D describes estimating the regularizer through averaged squared label-noise gradient differences, whereas Section 4 describes it as Hessian trace; preserve this measurement qualification.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
